patch_vs_full_margin_diagnostics.interpretation: Patch baselines are live current-arm forwards, not stored SFT selection values. Matching hashed prompt/token identities and current adapter identities rules out those semantic mismatches for newly bound caches. Patch passes use token-budgeted pair batches; full margins use batches of eight. The observed numerical-context differences also occur in fresh caches. Existing CPU artifacts do not isolate their cause or establish a numerical-noise floor for intervention effects.

scope.selection: Canonical SFT-v3 |effect| >= 0.5; seed 42; 64 pairs, gender 45; identical across all arms/seeds
scope.component_profile: Pearson across 64 real mixer/MLP suffix-patching effects
scope.head_rank: Descending signed real effect only among each run's AtP-selected plus control tested heads; not all-model rank
scope.head_ci: Existing candidate-bootstrap 95% CI is on share_removed, not logits per pair
scope.tail: p50/p99 of absolute logit effects across 450 aligned CV-job pairs per contrast; ratios to shared SFT; descriptive ranges, not CIs
scope.execution: HF interpretation loads the original Base and activates [SFT-v3, last-stage] adapters together; behavioral serving uses successively merged weights. Algebraic adapter addition is not evidence of numerical equivalence across these execution paths
scope.batch_context: Patch baselines and full-grid margins differ under their different batching contexts; see patch_vs_full_margin_diagnostics. Do not pool their per-pair margins as numerically interchangeable measurements
scope.inference: Replicated checkpoints on one development benchmark do not establish causal routes or external generalization. Neither p99 effects nor L23.H1 results identify the cause of high-hire-rate behavioral deterioration
